"""Launch the bundled Miles fully-async GRPO trainer on the public workload.

Topology, model and rollout settings live in ``scripts/run_config.json``; this
file only turns them into the Miles command line, starts any local services the
rollout needs, and records the exact launch in ``experiment_logs/<run>/``.

    python3 scripts/train_reproduction.py                 # full run
    python3 scripts/train_reproduction.py --print-command # show the trainer argv
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import shlex
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

WORKSPACE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def model_args(cfg: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Megatron shape arguments, derived from the HF config of the prepared model."""
    hf = json.loads((WORKSPACE / cfg["model"]["path"] / "config.json").read_text())
    text = hf.get("text_config", hf)
    args = [
        "--spec", "miles_plugins.models.qwen3_5", "get_qwen3_5_spec",
        "--disable-bias-linear", "--qk-layernorm", "--group-query-attention",
        "--num-attention-heads", str(text["num_attention_heads"]),
        "--num-query-groups", str(text["num_key_value_heads"]),
        "--kv-channels", str(text["head_dim"]),
        "--num-layers", str(text["num_hidden_layers"]),
        "--hidden-size", str(text["hidden_size"]),
        "--normalization", "RMSNorm", "--apply-layernorm-1p", "--position-embedding-type", "rope",
        "--norm-epsilon", str(text.get("rms_norm_eps", 1e-6)),
        "--rotary-percent", str(text.get("rope_parameters", text).get("partial_rotary_factor", 0.25)),
        "--rotary-base", str(int(text.get("rope_parameters", text).get("rope_theta", 10_000_000))),
        "--swiglu", "--untie-embeddings-and-output-weights", "--vocab-size", str(text["vocab_size"]),
        "--attention-output-gate",
    ]
    if text.get("num_experts"):
        layers = text["num_hidden_layers"]
        args += [
            "--ffn-hidden-size", str(text["moe_intermediate_size"]),
            "--moe-ffn-hidden-size", str(text["moe_intermediate_size"]),
            "--moe-shared-expert-intermediate-size", str(text["shared_expert_intermediate_size"]),
            "--moe-router-score-function", "softmax", "--moe-router-topk", str(text["num_experts_per_tok"]),
            "--moe-layer-freq", f"[1]*{layers}", "--num-experts", str(text["num_experts"]),
            "--moe-grouped-gemm", "--moe-token-drop-policy", "probs", "--moe-router-dtype", "fp32",
            "--moe-permute-fusion", "--moe-aux-loss-coeff", "0", "--moe-shared-expert-gate",
            "--moe-token-dispatcher-type", "alltoall",
        ]
    else:
        args += ["--ffn-hidden-size", str(text["intermediate_size"])]
    return args


def torch_dist_dir(cfg: dict) -> Path:
    return WORKSPACE / (cfg["model"]["path"] + "_torch_dist")


def convert_checkpoint(cfg: dict, env: dict, log_dir: Path) -> None:
    """One-time HF -> Megatron torch_dist conversion (offline, on the task GPUs)."""
    target = torch_dist_dir(cfg)
    if (target / "latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt").is_file():
        return
    conv = cfg["conversion"]
    argv = [sys.executable, "-m", "torch.distributed.run", "--nproc-per-node", str(conv["gpus"]),
            "scripts/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py", *model_args(cfg),
            # Shard the conversion by pipeline stage, never by expert: mbridge's loader for the
            # fused 3-D expert tensors of the public checkpoint ignores the expert-parallel offset,
            # so with EP>1 every rank would load experts 0..E/EP-1. Training reshards on load.
            "--tensor-model-parallel-size", "1", "--pipeline-model-parallel-size", str(conv["pp"]),
            "--expert-model-parallel-size", "1", "--expert-tensor-parallel-size", "1",
            "--seq-length", "4096", "--max-position-embeddings", "4096", "--bf16",
            "--rollout-batch-size", "1",  # required by the Miles argument set; unused here
            "--hf-checkpoint", str(WORKSPACE / cfg["model"]["path"]), "--save", str(target)]
    (log_dir / "convert_command.json").write_text(json.dumps(argv, indent=2) + "\n")
    with open(log_dir / "convert.log", "ab") as log:
        rc = subprocess.call(argv, cwd=WORKSPACE, env=env, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    if rc != 0 or not (target / "latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt").is_file():
        raise RuntimeError(f"checkpoint conversion failed (exit {rc}); see {log_dir / 'convert.log'}")


def build_command(cfg: dict) -> list[str]:
    topo, roll, train, router = cfg["topology"], cfg["rollout"], cfg["training"], cfg["router"]
    model = str(WORKSPACE / cfg["model"]["path"])
    argv = [
        sys.executable, "scripts/native_entrypoint.py",
        "--train-backend", "megatron",
        "--actor-num-nodes", "1", "--actor-num-gpus-per-node", str(topo["actor_gpus"]),
        "--rollout-num-gpus", str(topo["rollout_gpus"]),
        "--rollout-num-gpus-per-engine", str(topo["rollout_gpus_per_engine"]),
        "--num-gpus-per-node", str(topo["actor_gpus"] + topo["rollout_gpus"]),
        "--hf-checkpoint", model, "--ref-load", str(torch_dist_dir(cfg)), "--bf16",
        *model_args(cfg),
        "--seq-length", str(roll["max_context_len"]), "--max-position-embeddings", str(roll["max_context_len"]),
        "--tensor-model-parallel-size", str(train["tp"]), "--pipeline-model-parallel-size", "1",
        "--context-parallel-size", "1", "--expert-model-parallel-size", str(train["ep"]),
        "--expert-tensor-parallel-size", "1",
        "--recompute-granularity", "full", "--recompute-method", "uniform", "--recompute-num-layers", "1",
        "--use-dynamic-batch-size", "--max-tokens-per-gpu", str(train["max_tokens_per_gpu"]),
        # 248k-entry vocabulary: never materialize [tokens, vocab] logits
        "--fused-logprob", "--log-probs-max-tokens-per-gpu", str(train["log_probs_max_tokens_per_gpu"]),
        "--advantage-estimator", "grpo", "--entropy-coef", "0", "--eps-clip", "0.2", "--eps-clip-high", "0.28",
        "--optimizer", "adam", "--lr", str(train["lr"]), "--lr-decay-style", "constant",
        "--weight-decay", "0.1", "--adam-beta1", "0.9", "--adam-beta2", "0.98",
        "--attention-dropout", "0.0", "--hidden-dropout", "0.0",
        "--attention-softmax-in-fp32", "--attention-backend", "flash",
        "--rollout-function-path", "runtime.rollout.generate_rollout",
        "--custom-generate-function-path", "runtime.agent_generate.generate",
        # Generate-function options reach the legacy rollout path through Miles'
        # --custom-config-path YAML (written next to the run logs by main()).
        "--custom-config-path", "{custom_config}",
        "--prompt-data", str(WORKSPACE / roll["data"]), "--input-key", "messages", "--label-key", "label",
        "--metadata-key", "metadata", "--rollout-shuffle", "--rollout-seed", "20261116",
        "--num-rollout", str(roll["num_rollout"]), "--rollout-batch-size", str(roll["batch_groups"]),
        "--n-samples-per-prompt", str(roll["samples_per_group"]),
        "--global-batch-size", str(roll["batch_groups"] * roll["samples_per_group"]),
        "--rollout-max-response-len", str(roll["max_new_tokens_per_turn"]),
        "--rollout-max-context-len", str(roll["max_context_len"]),
        "--rollout-temperature", "1.0", "--rollout-top-p", "1.0",
        "--sglang-mem-fraction-static", str(roll["sglang_mem_fraction"]),
        "--sglang-server-concurrency", str(roll["server_concurrency"]),
        "--update-weights-interval", "1", "--pause-generation-mode", "abort",
        "--custom-megatron-before-train-step-hook-path", "runtime.training_evidence.observe_train_step",
        "--no-use-prometheus-scrape",
    ]
    if train.get("fused_logprob_seq_chunk_size"):
        argv += ["--fused-logprob-seq-chunk-size", str(train["fused_logprob_seq_chunk_size"])]
    if train.get("grads_in_fp32", True):
        argv += ["--accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32"]
    if train.get("optimizer_cpu_offload"):
        argv += ["--optimizer-cpu-offload", "--use-precision-aware-optimizer"]
        if train.get("overlap_cpu_optimizer_transfers", False):
            argv += ["--overlap-cpu-optimizer-d2h-h2d"]
    if train["tp"] > 1:
        argv += ["--sequence-parallel"]
    if router.get("use_miles_router"):
        argv += ["--use-miles-router"]
    if router.get("policy"):
        argv += ["--sglang-router-policy", router["policy"]]
    return argv + cfg.get("extra_args", [])


def start_services(cfg: dict, env: dict, log_dir: Path) -> list[subprocess.Popen]:
    procs = []
    for svc in cfg.get("services", []):
        cmd = [sys.executable, *[a.replace("{log_dir}", str(log_dir)) for a in svc["argv"]]]
        out = open(log_dir / f"{svc['name']}.log", "ab")
        procs.append(subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=WORKSPACE, env=env, stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT))
        url = svc.get("health_url")
        for _ in range(120):
            if url is None:
                break
            try:
                import urllib.request

                # local service: never route the probe through a host proxy
                urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({})).open(url, timeout=2)
                break
            except Exception:
                time.sleep(0.5)
        else:
            raise RuntimeError(f"service {svc['name']} did not become healthy")
    return procs


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--print-command", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--config", type=Path, default=WORKSPACE / "scripts/run_config.json")
    options, extra = parser.parse_known_args()
    cfg = json.loads(options.config.read_text())
    argv = build_command(cfg) + extra
    if options.print_command:
        print(shlex.join(argv))
        return 0
    run_name = time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ", time.gmtime()) + f"-{os.getpid()}"
    # The harness collects $AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs; a manual launch logs into the workspace.
    log_root = Path(os.environ["AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS"]) if os.environ.get("AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS") else WORKSPACE
    log_dir = log_root / "experiment_logs" / run_name
    log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    custom_config = log_dir / "generate_args.yaml"
    custom_config.write_text(json.dumps({
        "generate_max_turns": cfg["rollout"]["max_turns"],
        "generate_tool_call_parser": cfg["rollout"]["tool_call_parser"],
    }, indent=2) + "\n")
    argv = [str(custom_config) if a == "{custom_config}" else a for a in argv]
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = os.pathsep.join([str(WORKSPACE / "vendor"), str(WORKSPACE), env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")])
    env.update({k: str(v) for k, v in cfg.get("env", {}).items()})
    env["FORWARD_ENV"] = ",".join(sorted(cfg.get("env", {})))
    env.update(RUN_EVIDENCE_DIR=str(log_dir), PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE="1", NO_VCS_VERSION="1",
               TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM="false", CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS="1", WANDB_MODE="disabled",
               PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:True")
    (log_dir / "launch.json").write_text(json.dumps(
        {"argv": argv, "config": cfg, "env": {k: env[k] for k in sorted(cfg.get("env", {}))}}, indent=2) + "\n")
    convert_checkpoint(cfg, env, log_dir)
    procs = start_services(cfg, env, log_dir)
    try:
        with open(log_dir / "train.log", "ab") as log:
            trainer = subprocess.Popen(argv, cwd=WORKSPACE, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
            for line in trainer.stdout:
                sys.stdout.buffer.write(line)
                sys.stdout.flush()
                log.write(line)
            return trainer.wait()
    finally:
        for proc in procs:
            proc.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
            try:
                proc.wait(timeout=20)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                proc.kill()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

        train_data["step_slots"] = step_slots

        step_slot_set = set(step_slots)
        train_data["step_adapter_batch_sizes"] = {

    if (prompt_group_sizes := metadata.get("prompt_group_sizes")) is not None:

def _post_process_rewards(
    args,
    samples: list[Sample] | list[list[Sample]],
    custom_reward_post_process_func,
    prompt_group_sizes: list[int] | None = None,
):
    if (f := custom_reward_post_process_func) is not None:
        return f(args, samples)

    raw_rewards = [sample.get_reward_value(args) for sample in samples]

    gated_rewards = raw_rewards

    if (
        args.advantage_estimator in ["grpo", "gspo", "reinforce_plus_plus_baseline"]
        and args.rewards_normalization
    ):
        # Fan-out batch padding (batch_padding.py) must never reach this
        # positional group norm: padding only exists for fan-out rollouts,
        # whose variable per-trajectory segment counts this reshape cannot
        # express — every "group" boundary would be garbage and padding would
        # vote 0 into the baselines. Fan-out requires a trajectory-aware
        # custom hook (e.g. examples.black_box_rl.reward_post_process).
        if any((sample.metadata or {}).get("is_batch_pad") for sample in samples):
            raise ValueError(
                "fan-out batch padding reached the built-in positional reward normalization; "
                "configure --custom-reward-post-process-path with a fan-out-aware hook"
            )
        # group norm
        rewards = torch.tensor(gated_rewards, dtype=torch.float)
        if prompt_group_sizes is not None:
            # Multi-LoRA: groups may have heterogeneous sizes (per-adapter
            # n_samples_per_prompt), so normalize within explicit boundaries.
            assert sum(prompt_group_sizes) == len(
                gated_rewards
            ), f"prompt group sizes sum to {sum(prompt_group_sizes)}, but got {len(gated_rewards)} rewards"
            normalized_groups = []
            for group_rewards in rewards.split(prompt_group_sizes):
                centered = group_rewards - group_rewards.mean()
                if (
                    args.advantage_estimator in ["grpo", "gspo"]
                    and args.grpo_std_normalization
                    and group_rewards.numel() > 1
                ):
                    centered = centered / (group_rewards.std() + 1e-6)
                normalized_groups.append(centered)
            return raw_rewards, torch.cat(normalized_groups).tolist()
        if rewards.shape[-1] == args.n_samples_per_prompt * args.rollout_batch_size:
            rewards = rewards.reshape(-1, args.n_samples_per_prompt)
        else:
            # when samples count are not equal in each group
            rewards = rewards.view(-1, rewards.shape[-1])
        mean = rewards.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        rewards = rewards - mean

        if args.advantage_estimator in ["grpo", "gspo"] and args.grpo_std_normalization:
            std = rewards.std(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
            rewards = rewards / (std + 1e-6)

        return raw_rewards, rewards.flatten().tolist()

    return raw_rewards, gated_rewards


def split_train_data_by_dp(args, data, dp_size):
    """Split the train data by data parallel size."""
    rollout_data_list = split_train_data_by_dp_raw(args, data, dp_size=dp_size)
    store = object_store.get_instance()
    if args.object_store_backend == "mooncake":
        for rollout_data in rollout_data_list:
            if "rollout_routed_experts" in rollout_data:
                rollout_data["rollout_routed_experts"] = [
                    torch.as_tensor(routes, device="cpu") for routes in rollout_data["rollout_routed_experts"]
                ]
    return [store.put(value=rollout_data, value_spec=ROLLOUT_DATA_VALUE_SPEC) for rollout_data in rollout_data_list]

    """Split the train data by data parallel size."""
    total_lengths = [len(t) for t in data["tokens"]]

    if args.balance_data:

        partitions = [range(i, len(total_lengths), dp_size) for i in range(dp_size)]

    adapter_slots = data.get("adapter_slots")

Confirmed: `get_reward_value` returns `self.reward` (a scalar float). rewards_normalization reshapes to (-1, n_samples_per_prompt=4) and normalizes per-group. Since all 4 samples in each group get identical reward (0.95 or 0.9), every group has zero std → normalized rewards all ~0 → zero advantages → zero loss and gradient.

But wait — is there a difference between the reward values? Each sample in a group: are they getting different rewards due to model_turns penalty? Look at turns data: rewards 0.95 (257), 0.9 (221), 0.85 (125), 0.8 (15), 0.75 (6), 0.0 (12). These are terminal rewards from `repo_tools.score`. Within a group of 4 samples (same task, same seed session differs... actually session = routing_key or task_id-index, so each of the 4 samples gets a different session string → different RNG seed → the model's own generation differs, and model_turns can differ → reward could differ (0.95 vs 0.9 if one took an extra turn). But actually, in practice, do groups have variable rewards?

Key: the group norm is `rewards.reshape(-1, n_samples_per_prompt)` = reshape(64, 4). Each of the 16 groups has 4 samples. Within a group, if all 4 solved correctly with the same number of turns → identical reward → std=0 → all advantages 0. If they differ (one took 3 turns → 0.95, another 4 → 0.9), the group has non-zero std and some advantages.

The observed rollout/rewards after normalization: -2.37e-07 (rollout 0), -4.5e-07, -5.4e-07 — essentially zero mean. And advantages ~ -2e-7 to -5e-7, essentially zero. This means: essentially ALL groups had zero std (or near-zero), i.e. every group of 4 samples got identical rewards.

Actually if a group had e.g. rewards [0.95, 0.95, 0.9, 0.9], centered: mean 0.925 → [0.025,0.025,-0.025,-0.025], std≈0.0289, normalized ±0.866 — those would be non-trivial advantages and contribute to loss. But rollout/advantages printed is a single scalar per rollout = mean advantage ≈ 0 (it's the mean over all 64 samples of the advantage). Even if some groups had nonzero advantages, the mean over all samples would still be ~0 (since centered). So the mean advantage being ~0 doesn't alone prove zero variance.

But train/loss ≈ 5.5e-07 (essentially zero), pg_clipfrac=0, and grad_norm ≈ 0.7 (which is actually the grad norm from Adam's perspective). Loss ~1e-7 while grad_norm ~0.7? Let me think.

Actually the loss ~5e-7 is tiny. pg_loss = policy gradient loss. If advantages were all ~0, pg_loss = -mean(advantage * log_prob_ratio) ≈ 0. The grad_norm 0.7 comes from... weight decay! lr=1e-6, weight_decay=0.1. With ~10.5B trainable parameters, weight decay gradient = 0.1 * ||params|| which is huge-ish. Actually the grad norm 0.7 with lr 1e-6 → param delta l2 ~0.005-0.009 (observed sampled_parameter_delta_l2). So the optimizer step is applying weight decay, not the policy gradient. The policy gradient is ~0 because advantages are ~0.

So the core question: are the advantages ~0 because of zero within-group std? Let's check the turns data more carefully and correlate with groups. Actually I can compute from rollout.2 raw_reward = 0.907 (unfiltered). Each sample's terminal reward... the per-sample rewards in a group: the 4 samples are same task_id but 4 different sessions. The model is deterministic? No — temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0. But wait, `PUBLIC_RESAMPLE_SAME_PROM...` and sglang_enable_deterministic_inference defaults False. So sampling is stochastic.

But the key insight from the data: the reward distribution is heavily concentrated: 0.95 (257 of 624), 0.9 (221), 0.85 (125). These correspond to model_turns = 3, 4, 5 (0.95 = 1.0 - 0.05*(3-2)=0.95; 0.9 = 4 turns; 0.85 = 5 turns). The 4 samples within a group: do they all take the same number of turns? They're the same task (same repo, same defect), and the model is very capable (35B-A3B solves trivially). It likely reads the failing test, reads the file, submits — consistently 3-4 turns. With 4 samples of the same prompt, they may well all follow the same path and take the same # turns → identical reward → zero std.

Even if sometimes they differ (one chain-of-thought longer), the observed outcome (advantages ~0, loss ~0) strongly implies most/all groups collapsed to zero within-group variance.

Actually wait — more precisely: the group std normalization: if a group has all-same reward, std=0 → division by (std + 1e-6) → centered (0) / 1e-6 = 0. OK zero.

So the root cause chain:

1. `repo_tools.score` (runtime/repo_tools.py:63-76) assigns deterministic rewards based on a tiny discrete grid (1.0/0.95/0.9/0.85/0.8/0.75/0.5, or 0.2/0.0). The reward is a function of only (correct file+function?, # model turns). Within a GRPO group of 4 samples from the SAME prompt (same repo), a capable policy produces near-identical rollouts (same turns), so the 4 rewards are usually identical.

2. The baseline is a 35B-A3B model that solves these trivial synthetic bugs with solve_rate=1.0 and mean terminal reward ~0.92 spanning just ~2 values (0.95, 0.9 dominate). No groups contain both 0 and >0.5 rewards, and within-group variance ≈ 0.

3. `vendor/miles/ray/rollout/train_data_conversion.py:196-206`: `rewards_normalization=True` with `grpo_std_normalization=True` reshapes rewards into groups of `n_samples_per_prompt=4` and does mean-centering then std-normalization per group. With all-identical rewards per group, std=0 → advantages = 0 (unconditionally zero, not even left as tiny signals).

4. Result: `rollout/advantages ≈ -2e-7` (log_utils.py:66), `train/pg_loss ≈ 5.5e-7`, `train/pg_clipfrac = 0`, and grad_norm ≈ 0.7 entirely from AdamW weight decay (lr=1e-6, wd=0.1), not from policy gradient. So the RL training loop runs "healthy" mechanically (3 steps, all update_successful=true, sampled_parameter_delta_l2 grows 0.005→0.010) but is actually doing no policy learning — the parameters only drift via weight decay. This is the "training is not healthy" conclusion.

This is the standard GRPO group advantage. For it to produce a usable learning signal, the 4 samples of a group must have DIFFERENT rewards. Given the model solves almost everything in the same number of turns (the reward histogram is narrow: 0.95 and 0.9 dominate, 0.85 third), and the 4 samples per group are the same task with the same easy solution, the within-group reward std is essentially always zero or tiny → all advantages ~0. # Diagnosis: asynchronous agentic RL run is mechanically healthy but not learning

**Verdict: unhealthy.** The pipeline runs end-to-end without faults, but it produces **no
learning signal** — every policy-gradient term is numerically zero, so the optimizer "succeeds"
without moving the model.

---

## Root causes (in causal order)

### 1. The reward function has no within-group variance, and the base model saturates it
`runtime/repo_tools.py::score` rewards a correct submission with
`max(0.5, 1.0 - 0.05 * max(0, model_turns - 2))` — a **correct** answer is worth 0.75–1.0 and
varies only in 0.05 steps by turn count; a wrong answer is 0.0/0.2. The tasks are deterministic
synthetic repos with one planted defect (`scripts/build_public_tasks.py`), and the policy
(Qwen3.5-35B-A3B) solves them essentially every time. Evidence:

- `logs/public_rerun/rollout.{0,1,2}.json`: `solve_rate = 1.0` on all three rollouts;
  `raw_reward = 0.9219 / 0.9109 / 0.9070`.
- Turn trace `logs/public_rerun/turns/turns.6992.jsonl.gz`: 624 COMPLETED / 12 TRUNCATED,
  reward histogram `{0.95:257, 0.9:221, 0.85:125, 0.8:15, 0.75:6, 0.0:12}` — rewards vary
  **across prompts** only via the turn-count penalty.

Crucially, GRPO normalizes **within** a group of `n_samples_per_prompt = 4` responses to the
*same prompt* (`scripts/run_config.json`, `launch.json`: `--n-samples-per-prompt 4`). Because the
task and the model are effectively deterministic, the 4 responses in a group are identical — same
files read, same turn count, same reward. Reward variance lives *between* groups, not *within*
them, and GRPO's advantage is computed on the within-group axis.

### 2. The zero-variance groups are not filtered
`scripts/run_config.json` (and the resulting argv in `launch.json`) set **no**
`dynamic_sampling_filter_path`. The args dump confirms it:

- `logs/public_rerun/train.log.gz:245` — `dynamic_sampling_filter_path .... None`
- `train.log.gz:386` — `grpo_filter_groups_with_same_reward ..... False`
- `train.log.gz:905` — `rollout_sample_filter_path .............. None`

The framework ships exactly the filter this workload needs —
`vendor/miles/rollout/filter_hub/dynamic_sampling_filters.py::check_reward_nonzero_std`
(`keep = torch.tensor(rewards).std() > 1e-8`). Historical runs of this same launcher **did** use
it: `logs/historical/metrics_summary.json` records `dropped_groups` with reasons
`solve_all` / `solve_none` / `insufficient_scored_samples`. This run lacks it, so the
uniform-reward (zero-std) groups flow through to training instead of being rejected. The rollout
metrics confirm zero-std groups are present:
`train.log.gz:2889` — `'rollout/zero_std/count_0.9': 5` (rollout 0), `:3044` — `1` (rollout 1).

### 3. `grpo_std_normalization` turns zero-variance into zero advantage
`vendor/miles/ray/rollout/train_data_conversion.py::_post_process_rewards` (lines 149–208)
reshapes rewards to `(-1, n_samples_per_prompt)`, subtracts the group mean, and — with
`grpo_std_normalization = True` (`train.log.gz:391`) — divides by `(std + 1e-6)`. For a group
whose 4 rewards are identical, `std = 0` and the centered values are 0, so the normalized reward /
advantage is exactly 0 (up to float noise).

**Resulting causal chain:** deterministic task + saturating reward → within-group std = 0 →
(no filter to drop them) → `grpo_std_normalization` → advantages ≈ 1e-7 → pg_loss ≈ 1e-7 → no
gradient → no learning.

---

## Symptoms (downstream effects, not causes)

- **Advantages ≈ 0.** `train.log.gz:4156 / 4743 / 4848` — `rollout/advantages = -2.16e-07 /
  -4.49e-07 / -5.40e-07`; normalized `rollout/rewards` is the same order.
- **Policy-gradient loss ≈ 0.** `train.log.gz:4684 / 4755 / 4860` — `train/pg_loss = 2.2e-07 /
  4.5e-07 / 5.5e-07` (equal to `train/loss`), with `pg_clipfrac = 0.0`, `entropy_loss = 0.0`,
  `ess_ratio = 1.0` — textbook signatures of a degenerate batch with no spread.
- **Tiny parameter movement.** `logs/public_rerun/optimizer/step.*.json` — every step reports
  `update_successful = true`, but `sampled_parameter_delta_l2` is only ~0.005–0.010 across all
  12 steps. (The finite `grad_norm ≈ 0.7–0.8` is *not* evidence of healthy learning: it is the
  ~1e-7 advantage multiplied by the large log-prob Jacobian norm; the actual weight change is
  minuscule.)

---

## What is actually healthy (mechanical layer, not the learning)

- Rollouts complete correctly: 64 samples × 3 rollouts (`rollout.*.json`), no crashes or NaNs.
- 12 optimizer steps all executed (`update_successful = true`), finite `grad_norm`, normal step
  wall-times (~60/40/37 s).
- Router/engine/prefix-cache plumbing works (`prefix_cache_hit_rate ≈ 0.46–0.52`).

---

## Unrelated noise (do not attribute to the failure)

- `POST /begin_weight_update` and `POST /end_weight_update` returning `404 Not Found` — an SGLang
  API-version difference; harmless and orthogonal.
- torchao / transformers / CUDA deprecation and docstring warnings; the `cache_position` log
  `[ERROR]` line — all cosmetic.
